blockers: Stage-1 stratum labels are wrong for a material share of UNSOLVED problems, so 'UNSOLVED = both attempts wrong / problems the judge could not solve' (main.tex:19, :51, :73) is false as stated. Hand review (hand_checks.csv) covered only the 22 grader A/B disagreements; every problem on which both graders marked a reply wrong was accepted unchecked, and both graders reject correct answers that carry a 'name(args)=' prefix or a trivial rewrite, even though the same prefix was accepted by hand in 22 of 22 disagreements (e.g. 'C =', 'p =', 'm =' in hand_checks.csv). Reading all 90 UNSOLVED replies in exps/c3/raw/solve against the official gold in pools.json, I find at least 13 haiku-UNSOLVED problems where BOTH replies equal the gold (arxivmath-0126_14, 0126_4, 0226_11, 0226_19, 0226_22, 0426_14, 0426_22, 0526_1, 0526_10, 0526_19, 0526_20, 0526_28, smt_2025_50; 0126_7 differs only by log vs ln) and 6 more where one reply is correct (0126_16, 0226_9, 0326_29, 0426_17, 0426_18, 0526_24), so about 20 of 90 are SOLVED or MIXED by the preregistered definition. The paper's sentence 'all [22] were equivalent forms' (main.tex:51) is true but implies the stratification was verified, which it was not. Effect of correcting: haiku H1u survives (dU +0.27 [+0.14,+0.40], n=70 vs paper +0.24 [+0.13,+0.36], n=90; dS +0.07, n=151; interaction b +0.125, se 0.086, one-sided p 0.073 vs 0.065), so the headline is robust, but the stratum definition, the counts (137/90) and the sample sizes must be corrected or the misgrading disclosed and a re-graded sensitivity analysis reported. Misgrades also leak into MIXED (e.g. arxivmath-0626_28 both replies equal gold; 0426_36 attempt 2 uses a Unicode minus), which dropped problems that should have been SOLVED.
non_blocking: Contribution (2) says a forced pick selects 'exactly the wrong solution the same judge's verification passes most' (main.tex:30). The tested quantity h is the mean ISO-accept of the picked candidate minus the mean of the other two (+0.19 on UNSOLVED, +0.02 on SOLVED); it is not an argmax claim. Reword to 'accepted more often than the pool's other wrong solutions'.

The abstract and Section C3 say the penalty is confirmed on problems the judge cannot solve but that specificity is not established; this is fairly worded. However 'the same two confirmed effects' for sonnet (main.tex:19) should state that strata are haiku-defined and that sonnet H1u/H2u were labelled exploratory-confirmatory in A1; the body does say so, the abstract does not.

H3 is inconclusive (diff +0.016 [-0.038,+0.069] in my recompute, upper bound above the +0.05 refutation margin), so 'did not reduce the selection effect' is correct but 'did not detectably' is the strongest permissible wording; do not read it as evidence of equivalence. The sentence 'the wrong solution a forced choice selects is also the one the other model is most likely to pass' is a post hoc descriptive: sonnet-verifier h_cross on haiku picks is +0.16 [+0.06,+0.27] on UNSOLVED but +0.01 [-0.01,+0.05] on SOLVED, so it should be stratified and labelled exploratory. The mirror analysis (sonnet picks, p about 0.042 to 0.049) was a descriptive in A1 and sits at the edge; do not call it a finding.

d compares one PICK call per pool with an OR over three ISO calls and different prompts; 'the pooled format added false choices' is a statement about this pairing, not about the lineup context alone. Defensible (it is conservative against the paper because ISO-any has three chances) but say so.

Unit of analysis is the problem and the ledger family structure (four hypotheses Holm, sonnet separate family, H3 single) matches PREREGISTRATION.md and A1; the gate rule was applied as written (parse 1.000, right-wrong 0.83-0.08, 137/90 per stratum). Holm values reproduce (H1 0.129 = 2 x 0.0647; H2s 0.128 raised to 0.129 by monotonicity). No deviation found except that the prereg promised a 150-per-stratum sample cap which was never triggered; all 227 selected.

Power was planned for SE about 0.064 but achieved SE(b) about 0.078 because only 6 contest problems are UNSOLVED (84 of 90 arXiv); the paper reports this, but should state the minimum detectable b (about 0.22) next to the inconclusive H1.

Mis-grading is one-directional (false negatives), which inflates the apparent difficulty of the arXiv family and shifts competence-versus-source confounding; the unreported UNSOLVED share by family after regrading should be reported.
One problem (arxivmath-0226_16) is UNRESOLVED because one SOLVE call is missing; correctly excluded and reported.
